_comment: Recall of our own relevance filter over the pools in ./fixtures-pool, which are captured BEFORE the filter runs. Regenerate deliberately (node scripts/reportPoolRecall.mjs --write-baseline) and review the diff — a floor that falls means the matcher started discarding products it used to keep. Never re-baseline to make a red build green.
_floorsComment: Per-query floors, so a change cannot raise the mean by helping easy queries while destroying one. A low floor can still mean the LABELS are generous rather than the filter wrong — freilandeier counts any plain egg — so read a floor against goldenSet.ts before raising the matcher to chase it.
_labelCorrectionComment: 2026-08-06, three changes the same day, measured separately and in this order. (1) LABELS corrected in goldenSet.ts, ranker untouched: meanRecall 0.871 -> 0.867, obst 1.00 -> 0.916, ruebli 0.265 -> 0.150. Those falls were not the filter getting worse — the DENOMINATORS grew to the honest set of products (obst went from 15 labelled relevant to 24; ruebli had been counting Rüebli biscuits, a cake, a juice and marzipan carrots as the vegetable). That exposed two real filter defects the bad labels had hidden. (2) RECALL fixed: HYPERNYMS conflated two lexical relations. It is directional so 'Apfel' cannot match a banana — correct for SIBLINGS — but 'rueebli' appeared only as a VALUE under gemuse and never as a key, so it expanded to nothing, and since an unrecognised token is mandatory that DISQUALIFIED every carrot. Rüebli and Karotte are one vegetable in two dialects, i.e. SYNONYMY, which is symmetric. Separate SYNONYM_GROUPS table (ISO 25964-1 keeps equivalence USE/UF apart from hierarchy BT/NT; Lucene has SynonymQuery apart from taxonomy rewrites), scored at the direct band 80/60 not the hypernym discount 40/30. meanRecall 0.867 -> 0.888, ruebli 0.150 -> 1.000, obst 0.916 -> 1.000, kartoffeln 0.859 -> 1.000. 'Apfel' -> 'Bananen' still 0, asserted by a test. (3) PRECISION fixed, and recall did not move at all — every floor in this file is byte-identical across it, which is the point: the rule DEMOTES, never excludes. The whole-name bonus granted 90 whenever the query word appeared anywhere in a name, so for 'Rüebli' the top five was a marzipan carrot, a Rörtli, a Kuchenstück, a Cake and a soup, all at 90, burying the actual Karotten at 80 — pool P@5 0.00 on a query with recall 1.000. The compound case was already right (Rüeblitorte scores 20 by the Right-hand Head Rule); the defect was multi-word titles, where German retail writes the type as a separate token. Fixed with PREPARED_TYPE_STEMS: if the name carries a prepared-type noun the query does not, cap at COMPOUND_MODIFIER_STRENGTH (20). This is product-type matching, approximated by a curated lexicon where industry uses a title tagger; capping rather than dropping is the two-stage cascade split (candidate generation keeps recall, ranking pays for precision). Pool P@5 0.941 -> 0.976 and obst P@5 reached 1.00 — the baby purée finally left rank 1, which is what the reverted band experiment had been chasing.
